L198: # FALCON
L199: 
L200: This is the code repository for the paper contributed to IEEE T-RO:
L201: 
L202: 【84†FALCON: Fast Autonomous Aerial Exploration using Coverage Path Guidance†ieeexplore.ieee.org】
L203: 
L204: Authors: 【85†Yichen Zhang†yzhangec.github.io】*, 【86†Xinyi Chen†xchencq.github.io】*, 【87†Chen Feng†chen-albert-feng.github.io】, 【88†Boyu Zhou†robotics-star.com】, and 【89†Shaojie Shen†uav.hkust.edu.hk】.
L205: This paper introduces FALCON, a Fast Autonomous aerial robot expLoration planner using COverage path guidaNce. FALCON effectively harnesses the full potential of online generated coverage paths in enhancing exploration efficiency. We also introduce a lightweight exploration planner evaluation environment that allows for comparing exploration planners across a variety of testing scenarios using an identical quadrotor simulator.
L206:

L204: # LS-MCPP
L205: 
L206: This repository is the benchmark and implementation of the algorithms for the graph-based multi-robot coverage path planning problem from the following two papers:
L207: 
L208:   * Branch master: *Jingtao Tang, Zining Mao, and Hang Ma. "Large-Scale Multi-Robot Coverage Path Planning on Grids with Path Deconfliction." T-RO. 【90†[paper]†arxiv.org】, 【91†[project]†sites.google.com】
L209:   * Branch aaai24: Jingtao Tang and Hang Ma. "Large-Scale Multi-Robot Coverage Path Planning via Local Search." AAAI 2024. 【92†[paper]†arxiv.org】, 【93†[simulation]†vimeo.com】, 【94†[project]†reso1.github.io】
L210: ## Installation
L211: 
L212: `pip install .`
L213: 
L214: ## Usage
L215: 
L216: Please refer to `demo.ipynb` and `demo_turn_min_mcpp.ipynb`.
L217: ## File Structure
L218:   * benchmark/
L219:     * instance.py: the class of MCPP instance
L220:     * plan.py: the class of plan (trajectories) for the robots
L221:     * simulation.py: a simple visualizer for MCPP execution animation
L222:     * solution.py: the class of the MCPP solution
L223:   * conflict_solver/
L224:     * high_level_planner.py: the high-level planner of priority-based search
L225:     * low_level_planner.py: the chaining, holistic (multi-label), and adaptive approaches for the low-level planner
L226:     * reservation_table.py: the reservation table of time intervals (for safe-interval path planning)
L227:     * states.py: state representations for the low-level planner
L228:   * data[optinal]:
L229:     * the accompanying simulation exp results for the paper (【95†download link†drive.google.com】).
L230:     * gridmaps: the 2d grid maps (partly from 【96†https://movingai.com/benchmarks/grids.html†movingai.com】)
L231:     * instances: the MCPP instances with roots and weights specified
L232:   * mcpp/
L233:     * disjoint_set.py: disjoint set data structure
L234:     * estc.py: the Extended STC algorithm
L235:     * graph.py: class of the decomposed graph
L236:     * local_search.py: the proposed local search framework for MCPP
L237:     * operator.py: the three boundary editing operators
L238:     * planners.py: MCPP planner wrappers
L239:     * pool.py: class of operator pool
L240:     * rooted_tree_cover.py: implmentation of Even, Guy, et al. "Min–max tree covers of graphs." OR-L'04
L241:     * utils.py: utility functions
L242:   * turn_minimization/

L16: > Abstract:Line coverage is the task of servicing a given set of one-dimensional features in an environment. It is important for the inspection of linear infrastructure such as road networks, power lines, and oil and gas pipelines. This paper addresses the single robot line coverage problem for aerial and ground robots by modeling it as an optimization problem on a graph.
L17: The problem belongs to the broad class of arc routing problems and is closely related to the rural postman problem (RPP) on asymmetric graphs. The paper presents an integer linear programming formulation with proofs of correctness. Using the minimum cost flow problem, we develop approximation algorithms with guarantees on the solution quality. These guarantees also improve the existing results for the asymmetric RPP.
L18: The main algorithm partitions the problem into three cases based on the structure of the required graph, i.e., the graph induced by the features that require servicing. We evaluate our algorithms on road networks from the 50 most populous cities in the world, consisting of up to 730 road segments. The algorithms, augmented with improvement heuristics, run within 3s and generate solutions that are within 10% of the optimum. We experimentally demonstrate our algorithms with commercial UAVs.
